INCIDENT SUMMARY
A waxy crude oil spill resulted from an unlatched top hatch on a transport vehicle, resulting in a spill approximately seven miles long that started in
Duchesne at the Main Street and 100 West and concludes on the west side of the bridge over Starvation Reservoir. The crude oil does not flow and is
contained to the road. Currently, it has not impacted the soils next to the road, a waterway, a storm drain, or a dry drainage. Utah Highway Patrol is
blocking traffic to prevent vehicles from driving through the spill. 
The volume is currently unknown and the spill is not consistent over the seven miles. 
The remediation response is in its early stages, with the contractor EMB on scene applying sand for absorption and will likely collect the sand and oil.
Further remediation efforts are being evaluated. 
No injuries have been reported. 
______________________________________________________________________________ 
Update 3/5/2026 at 11 pm - Savage Infrastructure has provided an update. 
The crude oil only spilled for five blocks west of the intersection of Main Street and 100 West, with some tracked further down the road by vehicles (not
spilled from the truck for seven miles as initially reported). There is no oil near the bridge near Starvation Reservoir. 
The oil has solidified, the widest part of the spill is 8 to 10 feet, and has not reached the edge of the road. There has been no impact to surface water or
storm drains. 
An additional third party remediation company, Enviro Care is enroute, and the project manager is Dirk Haywood, who can be reached at 801-698-8263.

was held in a detention pond after transfer from the Duchesne River. Recently, the line had been used to transport hydrocarbon-free production water.
However, any remaining hydrocarbon-free production water would have likely been removed by the approximately 24 hours of transfer of Duchesne
River water through the line from the detention pond. It is believed that the released water did not contain hydrocarbon-free production water. 
Antelope Creek, which is currently dry and about 5 miles from the Duchesne River, received the water. It is estimated the release traveled about 0.75
miles before soaking into the creek bed.

scheduled to take creek bottom and bank samples on December 18, 2024 to confirm the absence of contamination. For more information, contact
